title: VFX Emitter
description: Data-driven particle emitter. VFX are the highest-value visual work in this project and they are pure data + code, so contributors can add them without touching the engine or shipping any art. Emitters are triggered by sim events; the emitter itself is PRESENTATION ONLY and must never feed back into the deterministic sim.

trigger.description: What spawns this emitter. Every value but `ambient_idle` is a sim event. `ambient_idle` is presentation-only: the renderer spawns it on its own timer for units showing the idle clip, seeded from the presentation PRNG. It exists because idling is not an event and must not become one -- putting a cigarette in the deterministic simulation would widen the state the replay hash covers for something no outcome depends on. The renderer reads sim state and writes none, so invariant 4 holds.

layer.description: ground_decal is persistent battlefield state -- scorch, craters, rubble. Persistence is what makes a map look fought-over instead of freshly loaded.

persistent.description: If true, survives for the remainder of the mission. Only valid on ground_decal.

budget_priority.description: Culled first when the particle budget is exceeded. Muzzle flashes should outrank ambient dust.

hit_stop_ms.description: Presentation-layer freeze on impact. Sells weight. Never applied to the sim clock.

light.description: Transient light contribution. This is what makes muzzle flashes read at night and in thermal.

weapon_classes.description: Weapon classes this emitter serves, matched against WEAPON_CLASS in @lions/sim. Only meaningful when trigger is weapon_fire. Mirrors the audio manifest's weapon_classes field so presentation uses one vocabulary.

palette_ref.description: Palette key, e.g. 'vfx.fire' or 'dust.2'. Raw hex is rejected by CI -- the palette is the reason the game looks cohesive.

range.description: [min, max], sampled from the seeded presentation PRNG.

emit_over_ms.description: 0 = burst. >0 = sustained emission, for trails and fires.

direction_offset_deg.description: Rotates this layer's emission direction relative to the emitter's facing. 180 emits directly backwards -- an RPG or ATGM backblast, which is what identifies an AT team by the shape of its signature alone.

color_over_life.description: Stepped, not interpolated -- interpolation would generate off-palette colours. white_hot -> fire -> ember -> dust.3 is the canonical explosion ramp.

additive.description: Marks this layer as a hot, opaque core -- the three.js backend renders it fully opaque (alpha_over_life is ignored; the fragment always writes alpha 1.0) rather than fading it, so it reads as a solid patch of its resolved colour instead of diluting toward whatever is behind it. Reserve for vfx.white_hot-class effects (muzzle flashes, explosion cores). NOT a GPU additive/summing blend mode despite the name: overlapping additive particles do not sum brighter than a single one -- true additive blending was tried and rejected because it sums to colours no palette entry names (see packages/render/src/three/units/fx.ts's createParticleMaterial doc comment). Build a white-to-orange-to-red-orange grade by layering separate particle layers spatially (see fire_apfsds.json), not by relying on this field to blend one layer's colour past the palette.

heat_shimmer.description: Screen-space distortion pass. Reserve for burning wrecks and jet wash.

mesh_flash.description: Three.js backend only, and only once art/meshes/vfx/muzzle_flash.glb has loaded (the &mesh flag): this layer is superseded by a pooled, modelled flash mesh instead of being spawned as a particle. Falls back to the authored particle exactly as declared when the mesh has not loaded (mesh flag off, still loading, or the Pixi backend, which never reads this field). Reserve for a hot-core layer a modelled asset can shape better than stacked discs -- see packages/render/src/three/units/muzzle-flash.ts's own top comment.

mesh_burst.description: Three.js backend only, and only once art/meshes/vfx/explosion_burst.glb has loaded (the &mesh flag): this layer is superseded by a pooled, modelled explosion-fireball mesh instead of being spawned as a particle. Falls back to the authored particle exactly as declared when the mesh has not loaded (mesh flag off, still loading, or the Pixi backend, which never reads this field). The mesh_flash sibling field, for a structure_collapse/tunnel_collapse-triggered hot core rather than a weapon_fire one -- see packages/render/src/three/units/explosion-burst.ts's own top comment for why this attaches to structure_collapse specifically, not catastrophic_kill.
